newsitem.title: USA: Calif. business group calls for litigation reform.
newsitem.headline: Calif. business group calls for litigation reform.

text.p: California Chamber of Commerce said Thursday litigation reform was its top legislative priority for 1997.
"Our number one goal is to make sure the economy doesn't lose any ground," Allan Zaremberg, the chamber's executive vice president, told reporters at a briefing in Sacramento.

Zaremberg said the cost of litigation to companies was having a "chilling effect" on business expansion in the nation's most populous state. He added that litigation reforms would help to improve the state's job climate.

Fred Main, the chamber's vice president and general counsel, said litigation reform was necessary if California Gov. Pete Wilson hoped to move welfare recipients to work under new federal and state welfare rules.
The Chamber of Commerce said it would seek reforms to restrict and limit damage awards, change lawyer contingency fee arrangements and restrict product liability lawsuits.
